description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 from the fz-kdt.183 cold review (BLOCK), which turned this
ticket's open question into the prerequisite of the confluence arc.

THE FACT: list_element_type([]) is `none`, so once a recursive key keeps its
list element (fz-kdt.183) the seed rung `[]` keys list(none) (displays
empty_list()) and the first cons rung keys list(τ): every list accumulator
mints a 2-rung ladder and the frontier is the PRODUCT over accumulators.
Measured: partition/4 1 -> 4 keys ({empty_list(), list(int)}^2), split3/5
1 -> 8, split4/6 1 -> 16 (compile 18 -> 83 ms); seed the accumulator with [0]
instead of [] and the product vanishes (1 key). All four partition/4 bodies
are code-identical (16 differing canon lines, every one a static annotation;
lanes, reprs, instructions identical) -- a TRUNCATED LADDER (empty_list() ⊑
list(int)), the class drive_test.rs:10245 says fz-f98.14.10.2 retired. It is
already present at HEAD through TUPLE slots: 111 rungs over 25 fixtures
(Enum.reduce_while/3[.., {empty_list(), int}, ..] beside {empty_list(),
empty_list(), int} on 00420); element precision multiplies it 2.4x (269 / 44).

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN THE KEY FUNCTION: the reviewer's repair E'' (key the
empty rung as the position's address var instead of list(none)) renames the
rungs without merging them -- partition/4 still 4 keys. The fixpoint mints the
[] key BEFORE it learns τ; no function of the rung's own type can know the
rung above.

THE CURE (data-model up): key-level ABSORPTION/REBASE -- when a same-function
activation keyed list(τ) at a slot comes to exist, the activation keyed
list(none) at that slot is superseded: its rows fold into the standing one
(the analogue of ActivationInputAlternatives::insert_row's dominance,
semantic.rs:872-905, lifted from rows to KEYS), using Types::key_list_subsumes
(types/mod.rs:1163, today consulted only for callable surface candidates at
semantic.rs:556). fz-kdt.132's lesson applies exactly: a truncated ascent
ladder is not a subsumption problem to dedup at mint, it is a rung to
absorb once the rung above exists; fz-kdt.65/106's dominance absorption is
the precedent. Guard against fz-kdt.80's lesson (key equality != emission
idempotence): the absorbed key's executable must not be emitted.

RED-FIRST GATES (restated 2026-09-03 after research; the earlier "111 -> 0"
gate is UNACHIEVABLE and WRONG): absorption alone is a byte-exact no-op at
HEAD across all 469 products (no empty_list() reaches an Ignore position
until fz-kdt.183 keeps the element), and the HEAD rung population -- 53 pairs
over 15 fixtures by the distinct-key census -- is two populations: 30 code-
identical and 23 HONEST specializations on non-recursive keys (count/1
[empty_list()] compiles one clause, count/1[list(int)] two) that must stay.
So: partition/4 settles ONE activation on 00001_quicksort_plus_foo.fz WITH A
GROUND ELEMENT (display(inputs[2]) == "[int]") under 183's element precision
-- red under bare E' (4 keys); split3/5 and split4/6 (fx/) 1 key; 00420's E'-
created rungs 29 -> 6 and executables 238 -> 206; corpus executables with E'
5383 -> 5270 (below base's 5297); the quicksort schedule gate's bound stays
17; 0 behaviour movers on three doors; AND the frontier is a subscribable
FACT so a rung minted before its absorber is retired (FIFO/LIFO canon movers
0 -- the redirect-only prototype measures 3: 00183/00230/00419 keep four
{empty_list(), int} executables under LIFO only, and three public_trace
uncaused-evaluation gates stay honestly red until retirement lands).
MECHANISM (prototyped, proto124.diff): Types::rung_absorbs(hi, lo, mask) --
hi is lo with empty-list rungs filled at IGNORE positions only (an ignored
position's key part is list(joined element), so empty_list() there PROVES
every row held [] and folding blends nothing; unrestricted absorption was
measured RED, enum_map_family phantom +/2); empty_list() beside
non_empty_list(τ) is NOT a rung; rebuild-and-compare exactness; recursive
keys only. RETIREMENT: two designs refuted (silent -> 18 movers, the product
path wedges; forwarding -> 2 movers, a caller never re-keyed); the correct
shape is a per-(root, function) ACTIVATION-KEY ANTICHAIN published as a
fact, joined by antichain insertion under rung_absorbs, RESOLVED (read =
subscribed) by canonical_activation_key, so a frontier move re-runs the
caller, withdraws Activation(K_lo) and lets analyze_activation's unclaimed-
activation path retire the cone. Cold review pending on: the Ignore-only law,
the antichain fact, and how much of this population fz-kdt.183's demand-
through-forwarding rule never mints. BLOCKS fz-kdt.183.

comments.text: Data point from fz-kdt.132 (c31b309d0), which this ticket was named as a neighbour of. The take_drop 'cross-key subsumption smell' this ticket's neighbourhood was suspected of was NOT subsumption: the three same-function accumulator keys ({[], []}, {[], [int]}, {[], [int]} | {[int], []}) were a truncated ASCENT LADDER, not redundant siblings. Deduping them by containment would have been the wrong cure -- the right one minted the rung above them and the ladder collapsed to a single key on its own (three reducer specializations per captured lambda became one, 00420 215 -> 196 executables). Worth re-measuring 00277's Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] vs Kernel.dbg/1[list(int)] pair against HEAD before building: the population this ticket asks to count may have moved.

RE-MEASURED at d2a5f3510 (2026-09-02), head FIFO vs head LIFO: the Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] + fz_dbg_value/1[empty_list()] pair exists under LIFO only (beside dbg/1[list(int)] on both), and BOTH return `any` -- the fz-kdt.120 defect (a @spec variable bound to the whole `[]` argument is dropped by arrow_match.rs's empty-list ambiguity rule, so `dbg(t) :: t` at `[]` loses its result). FIFO carries its own one-schedule key instead: Range.reduce/5[..., {:cont, empty_list()}, ...]. So the population this ticket asks to count is, at head, two `[]`-keyed activations that a schedule mints when a callsite's argument is `[]` at an intermediate round and that survive beside the wider key. Sequence: after fz-kdt.120's rule lands (the `[]`-keyed dbg will then return `[]`, not `any`), re-count; what remains is the minting question this ticket owns, and fz-kdt.132's lesson applies (a truncated ascent ladder is not a subsumption problem).

title: The empty rung must fold at the key level: a list(none)-keyed activation is absorbed by the standing list(τ) activation of the same function, the way row dominance absorbs a superseded input row
